text:
Alex: FYI customer 'ProofPoint Health' (enterprise fintech-ish) wants a 2-week POC to validate conversational routing + automated case summarization. They asked: what are the success gates (latency/cost/quality), any enterprise blockers (KMS, VPC), and a rough cost burn estimate?
Sara: Quick q — what's their expected concurrency/peak? that'll drive model choice and Dedicated vs hosted.
Alex: Estimated steady 60 reqs/min with peaks ~180 reqs/min for short spikes. Average convo ~12 user turns, ~600 tokens per full convo. They want <400ms p95 for routing decisions and <800ms p95 for full summary generation ideally.
Maya: Security check — they require KMS-managed keys, VPC peering, and an SOC2 + SIEM-friendly audit stream. Do we already support full-key control for ephemeral POC data? @Tim?
Tim: We can run this in Redwood Dedicated in their VPC (private deployment) with customer KMS. For POC, ephemeral logs can be forwarded to their SIEM and we can disable persistent KV caching. Works fine. :thumbsup:
Alex: Acceptance criteria I'm proposing (draft):
- Functional: routing correctness >= 92% (measured by an eval set of 500 labeled chats)
- Summarization: ROUGE-L >= 0.62 OR human agreement >= 85% on 200 samples
- Latency: routing p95 <= 400ms; summary p95 <= 800ms under normal load
- Cost: steady-state inference cost <= $0.015 per 1k input tokens (POC estimate basis)
- Reliability: no more than 1 failure per 10k requests; successful fallback policy to smaller model if enriched model hits errors
Sara: For the eval set, do we have canonical prompts? Can you paste a few sample prompts so Eng-ML can wire up the eval harness?
Alex: Sure — sample prompt snippets: 
```
User: "Pull the relevant policy clauses from this conversation and summarize next steps for legal ops."
System: "You are a concise summarizer. Output JSON with keys: summary, action_items (list)."
```
```
User: "Customer reported duplicate transactions, give a short diagnostic and recommended troubleshooting steps."
System: "Return bullet list and severity score 1-5."
```
Maya: On data handling — they will pass PII. We need confirmation that no customer data persists beyond session unless explicitly stored, and that KMS keys control any stored artifacts.
Tim: Confirmed. For the POC we enable transient sessions, no persistent KV caching, and all blobs encrypted at rest with customer KMS. Also we can mask PII on ingest with a configurable redaction pipeline before storage.
Sara: Cost calc request: using Alex numbers — 6M tokens/day (10k conv/day x 600 tokens) -> how does that translate to rough $/day and projected POC burn for 14 days?
Tim: Quick calc: at $0.015 per 1k tokens -> 6,000k tokens/day * $0.015 = $90/day. 14 days -> ~$1,260 plus infra overhead (Dedicated reservation and egress). If we need lower cost we can try a quantized variant (4-bit) for summarization model; expect 20-30% token compute saving.
Alex: Also want to clarify fallback model: if primary model latency > 900ms or error rate > 1% for 5 min, route to lightweight model (quantized distill) with same prompt. Must be transparent to product (response includes "served_by").
Maya: Security questionnaire item: export controls, data residency (they need EU only), and incident response SLA. Can we scope POC to EU region and provide contact for IR escalation?
Tim: Yes EU region Dedicated available. I'll attach the IR contact and set up VPC peering runbook. deploy-bot: Reserved Dedicated slot (2xA10G) in eu-west-1 for 2026-04-12 09:00 UTC -> 2026-04-26 09:00 UTC.
Sara: Nice. Who's owning the POC runbook + test harness? I can own eval metrics pipeline if someone drafts the runbook.
Alex: I'll draft runbook skeleton today and ping eng-ml for eval harness wiring. @Tim can you confirm model variants and the canary policy for rollouts?
Tim: I'll post a small deploy config in the runbook: 
```
model: redwood/summarizer-quant4-v2
routing_model: redwood/routing-fast
autoscale: min_replicas:2 max_replicas:8 target_rps:120
fallback_policy: latency_threshold_ms:900 -> route:routing-light
kv_cache: disabled
encryption: kms_customer_key: "arn:aws:kms:eu:..."
```
Tim: Plan to run a 4-hour load test on day 2 of POC and iterate.
Alex: Next steps — finalize acceptance thresholds with ProofPoint by EOD tomorrow, sign off SOW, run security questionnaire answers, then spin up Dedicated reservation. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
